findings.evidence: `rg` hits show the new wrappers at `PermutationExtension.lean:30`, `:41`, `:76`; Mathlib has the replacement at `mathlib/Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Fintype.lean:156-160` (`theorem Perm.exists_extending_pair`). TauCeti uses only the wrappers at `ExchangeableAtMonotone.lean:46` and `FullyExchangeable.lean:61`; `exists_perm_extending_strictMono` has no TauCeti consumer.
findings.fix: Remove these declarations; in `ExchangeableAtMonotone.lean` use `Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair (Fin.castLE hmn) k (fun _ _ h => Fin.castLE_injective hmn h) hk`, in `FullyExchangeable.lean` use `Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair (fun i : Fin n => i.val) (fun i => (σ i).val) Fin.val_injective (fun _ _ h => σ.injective (Fin.val_injective h))`, and drop the unused strictMono wrapper or use the same theorem with `hk.injective` if needed.
findings.issue: `exists_perm_extending_castLE`, `exists_perm_extending_strictMono`, and `exists_perm_nat_extending_fin` duplicate Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair` as direct specializations.

summary: The new finite permutation-extension API is a set of public thin wrappers around an existing Mathlib theorem, with one wrapper unused in TauCeti. Reuse `Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair` directly at the two call sites and remove the duplicated declarations.
